title: SII Vol. 14 No. 3 — Tirupparankunram
location_detail: On one of the pillars in the rock-cut cave
summary: This Vatteuttu inscription dated in the 6th year of Maranjadaiyan which is engraved in arachaic letters, has been attributed to Jatila Parantaka of the Anaimalai inscription noted above

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 4 — Kuttalam
location_detail: On a pillar in the north-side of the Kurralanatha temple
summary: This incomplete record is dated in the 4th year and 360th day of the Pandya king Maranjadaiyan and mentions the gift of some donation by Maran-Achchan, probably a petty chieftain of Poliyur, for a lamp in the temple of Tirukurralattu-Bharata

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 5 — Tiruppattiru
location_detail: On the north wall of the Thiruttalisvara temple
summary: This bilingual inscription consists of a portion in Sanskrit and a portion in Tamil

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 6 — Aduturai
location_detail: On the north wall of the Apatsahayesvara temple
summary: This inscription of Maranjadaiyan of the year opposite to the year which was itself opposite to the fourth year of the king comes from Aduturai

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 7 — Aduturai
location_detail: On the south wall of the Apatsahayesvara temple
date_text: The significance of the regnal year, as cited here, instead of as 4 apposite to the year, is not clear
summary: This inscription also from Aduturai is peculiarly dated as 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1st year of the Pandya king Maranjadaiyan and relates to some provision for the supply of oil to the temple of Tirukkurangaduturai-Mahadeva by the sabha of Maruttuvakkudi in Tiraimur-nadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 8 — Kumbakonam
location_detail: On the west wall of the shrine of the goddess in the Nagesvara Temple
date_text: The regnal year of this inscription corresponds apparently to the year 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1, quoted in the Aduturai records (No. 7 above)
summary: This Tamil record dated in the 4 + 4th year of Maranjadaiyan registers a gift of 138 cows and 100 kasu by the king for the supply of milk and ghee and for maintaining two perpetual lamps in the temple of Bhatara of Tirukkilkottam in Tirukkudammukkur, i.e., Kumbakonam

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 9 — Tiruppattur
location_detail: On a slab in the first prakara of the Tiruttalisvara temple
date_text: This inscription of Maranjadaiyan is dated in the 4th year opposite to the 6th, which apparently is a wrong citation for 4 + 6th year
summary: The Sanskrit sloka at the beginning states that Patta, the daughter of Maran and the wife of Sankara donated 10 dinara for a lamp to the god Sristhalisa

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 10 — Tiruchichirappalli
location_detail: On the wall of the rock-cut cave
summary: This interesting inscription engraved in the Pallava rock-cut cave-temple on the hill at Tiruchichirappalli is dated in the 4th year and 2,501st day of the reign of king Maranjadaiyan, who is also called Pandyadhiraja Varaguna[varman]

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 11 — Tiruchichirappalli
location_detail: On a pillar in the upper rock-cut cave on the hill
summary: This record engraved in archaic Tamil characters with pullis marked for basic consonants, is dated in the 9th year opposite to the 4th year of the reign of Maranjadaiyan, who is referred to also as Pandyadhipati-Varaguna

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 12 — Tiruvellarai
location_detail: On the rock in front of the Jambunathasvami temple
summary: This record dated in the 9th year opposite to the 4th year of king Maranjadaiyan is important in that it contains a few astronomical details of its date, which are capable of verification, namely, Vrischika, Monday, Asvati

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 12 — Lalgudi
location_detail: On the north wall of the Saptarishisvara temple
summary: This inscription is dated in the year opposite to the fourth of some king whose name is not given in it

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 12 — Lalgudi
location_detail: On the north wall of the Saptarishisvara temple
summary: This record of Maranjadaiyan, alias Pandyakulapati Varaguna Maharaja registers the gift of l120 kasu by the king for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of Mahadeva at Tiruttavatturai Idaiyarru-nadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 13 — Ambasamudram
location_detail: On a slab built into the floor of the Erichchavudaiyar Temple
summary: This record dated in the 4 + 12th year of the reign of Varaguna-Maharaja registers the gift of 290 kasu to the sabhi of Ilangoykkudi in Mulli-nadu for worship and offerings to the God Bhatara in the Srikoyil of Tiruppottudaiyar

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 14 — Tiruchchirraambalam
location_detail: On the door-jamb of the Ardhamandapa of the Puratanavanesvara temple
date_text: The regnal year of the king namely, the 12th, opposite to the 4th, is also legible
summary: This record is very much damaged and only certain portions containing the name of the king, Varaguna-Maharaja and the name of the village, Tiruchchirremam are preserved

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 15 — Tiruppattur
location_detail: On a slab in the prakara of the Tiruttalisvara temple
date_text: This record belongs to the reign of the Pandya king Varaguna-Maharaja and is dated in the 4th year and 4635th day of his reign
summary: The pulli is marked in many consonants which fact proves its early date

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 16 — Tiruppattur
location_detail: On a slab lying in the Angalamman temple
summary: This record also comes from Tiruppattur and is dated in some year, which was probably  , and 4985th day of king Maranjadaiyan-s reign

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 16 — Tiruchchendur
location_detail: On two slabs setup in the Subrahmanyasvamin temple
summary: This inscription of Varaguna-Maharaja registers the gift by the king, of 1,400 kasu for meeting the various annual requirements of the temple of Subrahmany-bhatarar

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 17 — Vijayanarayanam
location_detail: On the south wall of the Manonmanisvara temple
summary: The subjoined inscription is dated in the 2nd year of Maranjadaiyan and registers that Panchavan-Pallavaraiyan alias Vel-Sendil of Korrampullankudi in Mudukudi-nadu purchased some lands from the sabha of Vijayanarayna-chaturvedimangalam, a brahmadeya in Nattarruppokku and gave them to the temples of

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 18 — Tirunelveli
location_detail: On the north wall of the Narasimha-Perumal temple
summary: This Vatteluttu record is dated in the 2nd year of the reign of Maranjadaiyan and registers a gift of cows made by Sattanammai, for burning a lamp in the temple of Brahmapurittevar at Tirunelveli, on behalf of Sattan-Deyam, a devaradiya of Tirunelvel in Kil-Vemba-nadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 19 — Tirukkurungudi
location_detail: On a stone belonging to the Nambi temple (now in the Madras Museum)
summary: This Vatteluttu inscription of Maranjadaiyan is dated in the 4th year and registers a sale by the mahasabhaiyar of Vaikuntha-valanadu in Nattarruppokku to Panchavan Brahmadhirajan alias Sendan-Sattan of Nellittola in Malai-nadu, who made it over to the temple of god Emberuman, who was pleased to be

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 20 — Trukkodikaval
location_detail: On the west wall of the Tirukkotisvara Temple
summary: This record is stated to be a copy of an earlier inscription dated in the 4th year of the reign of Maranjadaiyan and relates to the gift of 15 kalanju for burning a lamp in the temple of Tirukkodika-Mahadeva, by Araiyan-Kalvan of Panaiyur in Peraiyur-nadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 21 — Tirukkodikaval
location_detail: On the south wall of the Tirukkotisvara temple
summary: The record stated to be a copy of another inscription made during some repairs in the temple states that Varaguna-Maharajar endowed 180 kalanju of gold for burning from the interest thereon three perpetual lamps before the images of Sri Sarasvati and Ganapati in the temple at Tirukkodika alias Kanna

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 22 — Ayyampalaiyam
location_detail: Above the natural cave on the hill called Aivarmalai
date_text: The present epigraph yields A.D. 862-3 as the date of accession of Varaguna
summary: This Vatteluttu record which couples the 8th regnal year of king Varaguna with Saka 792 and the Anaimalai inscription of Jatila-Parantaka which is dated in the Kali era form the two important landmarks in early Pandya chronology

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 23 — Singampatti
location_detail: On a rock in a field at Melai-Singampatti
summary: This highly damaged Vatteluttu record belongs to the 8th year of the king Maranjadaiyan, but nothing more than his name can be traced in this inscription

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 24 — Tiruvisalur
location_detail: On the south wall of the Sivayoganatha temple
summary: This record which is built in at the right end is dated in the year opposite to the  th year of the reign of [Vara]guna-maharaja and appears to refer to some gift, the details of which are not available, to the god Tiruvisalur of Avaninarayana-chaturvedimangalam

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 25 — Tirugokarnam
location_detail: On the south wall of the Gokaranesvara temple
summary: This record dated in the 17th year of the reign of Maranjadaiyan registers a gift of gold by Varagunavadiyaraiyan alias Nakkan-Setti of Kalkurichchi in Kaviappal, a village in Valla-nadu
